done.why: The trap door was barred behind me, the east passage is unfinished, and the west hole and crawlway are blocked. I never found a key for the grating.

about: A cut-down Zork: the white house, kitchen, living room, a trap door to a cellar and a troll room. Unfinished passages carry notes from The Management, and something digs beyond a blocked crawlway.

moments.note: Leaflet could not be taken while I stood at the mailbox earlier, and the compass directions around the house were inconsistent.
The trap door crashed shut and was barred. The way back is gone.
The crawlway's digging sound stops politely until you back out.
The troll died in one blow and its carcass vanished in black fog.
A note pinned to the unfinished passage reads Back soon, The Management.

wished: A way back up from the cellar

lines.line: From somewhere beyond it comes the sound of digging, which stops, politely, until you have backed out.
The passage to the east has not been finished. A note is pinned to the rock: "Back soon. -- The Management."
lines.why: A playful way of marking the edge of the world.

lines.line: It is polished smooth by everything that has ever slid down it, and it is unclimbable.
lines.why: The added scenery prose is well written.

fun.why: Familiar opening, charming new bits, but it ends quickly.

engagement.why: Drive faded once everything was blocked.

difficulty.why: Little to solve, then a dead end that was not a puzzle.

interestingness.why: The remixed geography and the Management notes intrigue.

prose.why: New descriptions are witty and precise; the originals stay terse.
